title: The Life Is in the Blood

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'For the life of a creature is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for yourselves on the altar; it is the blood that makes atonement for one's life.'" - Lev 17:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here it is. The verse that explains everything.

Why blood? Why not grain, or gold, or good intentions? Because the life of a creature is in the blood. Blood is not a symbol chosen at random. It is life itself, poured out.

And notice the middle phrase, which is easily missed: I have given it to you. God gave this. Sacrifice was not a human invention to appease an angry deity — it was God's own provision, His idea, His gift to a people who could not otherwise come near Him.

That single phrase changes how we read the whole Old Testament. These altars were not humanity reaching up. They were God reaching down.

Hebrews draws the line from here: without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness (Heb 9:22). Sin costs a life. That is not cruelty; it is the seriousness of God's holiness and the reality of what sin destroys.

Which is why the cross is not a tragic accident but the fulfilment of everything this verse means. God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son (John 3:16). Again, God gave.

The life is in the blood — and Christ poured out His so that yours could be spared.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does it change things to know that God gave the sacrificial system as a provision?
2. Why does forgiveness require the cost of a life?
3. What does Christ's blood mean to you personally today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that atonement was never my idea but Your gift. Thank You that Christ poured out His life so that mine could be spared. I will never deserve it. Amen.
